readme:
# cardputer-puzzles

**All 40 of Simon Tatham's puzzles on the M5Stack Cardputer ADV: flash one
`.bin` and play offline.**

![Cardputer ADV running the puzzle picker](docs/hero.jpg)

Simon Tatham's Portable Puzzle Collection ported to the **M5Stack Cardputer ADV** (ESP32-S3 Stamp-S3A).

Upstream project: https://www.chiark.greenend.org.uk/~sgtatham/puzzles/

## Included games (40)

Simon Tatham's collection, alphabetical:

Black Box · Bridges · Cube · Dominosa · Fifteen · Filling · Flip · Flood ·
Galaxies · Guess · Inertia · Keen · Light Up · Loopy · Magnets · Map · Mines · Mosaic ·
Net · Netslide · Palisade · Pattern · Pearl · Pegs · Range · Rectangles ·
Same Game · Signpost · Singles · Sixteen · Slant · Solo · Tents · Towers ·
Train Tracks · Twiddle · Undead · Unequal · Unruly · Untangle

> Any game that runs out of memory shows an error and reboots to the menu
> rather than hanging.

## Hardware

- M5Stack Cardputer ADV (ESP32-S3 Stamp-S3A, 8 MB flash, **no PSRAM**)
- 240x135 display
- Primary / tested target: Cardputer ADV

### Original (non-ADV) Cardputer

Built and tested on the **ADV**. It should run on the original Cardputer too: there
are no ADV-only code paths, M5Unified picks the keyboard driver at runtime, and both
boards are StampS3 with 8 MB flash and the same 240x135 panel. The tilt pointer needs
the IMU the ADV added, so it stays off there; cursor mode is the default anyway.

Untested on that board. Two things would most likely need a nudge: the Fn-modified
keycodes behind the `; . , /` cluster, and the idle light-sleep path (its wake logic
was reasoned against the ADV's keyboard controller). Neither should crash; worst case
a key does the wrong thing. **If you try it, open an issue saying what the Fn keys do**
and it can be fixed properly.

## Install (prebuilt)

**Easiest: [flash it from your browser](https://chongjiazhen.github.io/cardputer-puzzles/#install)**
- plug the Cardputer in over USB-C and press one button. Desktop Chrome or Edge only
(Web Serial), and the write skips the `nvs` partition so an upgrade keeps your
in-progress games.

Or grab a `.bin` from the [latest release](../../releases/latest) - no toolchain needed.
Both assets carry the version in the name (`…-vX.Y-…`); a flashed device also shows it
in the `Tab`→Help screen.

- **Full flash (recommended)** - `cardputer-puzzles-vX.Y-merged.bin`, written at offset `0x0`.
  Self-contained (bootloader + partition table + app) and the only path that guarantees
  **save-state persistence**, since it installs the LittleFS data partition this firmware
  expects. Flash via [M5Burner](https://docs.m5stack.com/en/download) ("Custom firmware"),
  a web flasher, or esptool:
  ```sh
  esptool --chip esp32s3 write-flash 0x0 cardputer-puzzles-vX.Y-merged.bin
  ```
- **App-only** - `cardputer-puzzles-vX.Y-app.bin`, for OTA / SD-card launchers such as the
  [M5Stack Launcher](https://bmorcelli.github.io/Launcher/). Runs fine, but it keeps the
  device's existing partition table - resume/persistence works **only** if that table has a
  `spiffs` data partition. For guaranteed persistence, use the full-flash bin above.

## Building and flashing

```sh
# Clone with submodule (game logic lives in upstream/)
git clone --recurse-submodules <repo-url>
cd cardputer-puzzles

# Or, after a plain clone:
git submodule update --init

# Build and flash
pio run -e puzzles -t upload
```

Requires [PlatformIO](https://platformio.org/) and the ESP32 toolchain (installed automatically by PlatformIO on first build). No secrets or network config - the puzzles run fully offline.

### Host tests

```sh
scripts/host-tests.sh          # all of them
scripts/host-tests.sh smear    # one, by name fragment
```

Needs gcc/g++ with C11 and C++17, and nothing else: no PlatformIO, no device.
`startgame_test` walks the full midend lifecycle (new game, size, redraw, free)
for all 40 games; `smear_test` renders the device's actual draw policy against a
from-scratch reference and compares every frame; the rest cover key mapping, the
tilt pointer, and the bug-report URL. Everything compiles into a temp directory,
so a failed run cannot leave a stale binary behind for the next one to pass on.

`frontend.cpp` and `main.cpp` are device-only (they need M5GFX), so render and
input changes still need a flash and a look at the screen.


## Controls

Every plain key goes to the puzzle (so games that use letters - Map's `l`,
Solo's hex digits, etc. - work). Frontend commands live on Ctrl, Tab, and `` ` ``.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `;` `.` `,` `/` | Move cursor (up / down / left / right) |
| `Enter` | Select (cursor cell, or click at the crosshair in pointer mode) |
| `Space` | Select2 / mark (flag, pencil, …) |
| digits / letters / `⌫` | Per-game input |
| `Ctrl`+`Z` / `Ctrl`+`Y` | Undo / Redo |
| `Ctrl`+`N` / `Ctrl`+`R` | New game / Restart |
| `Tab` | **Menu** (in game: size/type, new, restart, solve, undo/redo, pointer, recenter, zoom, pan, rules, report bug) · **Help / Settings** (on the game list) |
| `Ctrl`+`P` | Toggle the IMU tilt pointer (then Enter/Space act at the crosshair) |
| `Ctrl`+`Space` | Recenter the tilt pointer - set the current hold as neutral (works at any posture) |
| `Ctrl`+`L` | Toggle 2× zoom - play continues magnified; `Ctrl`+`;` `.` `,` `/` pans the view |
| `Ctrl`+`F` | Star the highlighted game (game list only) - starred titles pin to the top |
| `` ` `` | Back (to the game list / out of a menu) |

**Drag games** - Map, Pegs, Signpost, Guess and Untangle - move something from
one place to another. In pointer mode the crosshair cannot hold a button, so the
drag is split across two presses: `Enter` picks up, tilt to aim, `Enter` drops.
`Space` is the second channel (Map's pencil, Untangle's edge toggle) and works
the same way. **The key that picked it up is the key that drops it; the other key
cancels.** While you are carrying something the crosshair becomes a box with a
centre dot.

The game list and menus are a scrolling picker: `;`/`
